resale_co.name: Resale Certificate / Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), Residential
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Woodcliff Lake Building Department (Construction/Zoning Official), with Fire Prevention
resale_co.lead_time: Submit the form no less than 20 days before the closing date. The Borough inspects within 10 business days after the application is complete and permits are verified closed.
resale_co.valid_for: The application form says 90 days from issuance; the Borough code (Section 135-3, amended 2024) says six months
requirements: All construction permits issued must be closed out before the inspection
Legible house numbers clearly visible from the street
Sump pumps not piped into the sanitary sewer system and discharged properly
Boilers, hot water heaters and water softeners must have had the required permits
Front door dead bolts keyless on the interior side
Damaged or uneven public sidewalks and aprons must be replaced (permit required)
Smoke detector, carbon monoxide detector and portable fire extinguisher installed (code and form still list the extinguisher)
Secondary power sources (generators, solar, batteries) need a printed CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER label within 18 inches of the main panel and the meter
Monitored or low-voltage alarm systems must pass an alarm test with monitoring active

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Application - Certificate of Continued Occupancy - Residential (posted under Fire Prevention forms) and submit it to the Borough of Woodcliff Lake, 188 Pascack Road, at least 20 days before closing, with the fee. The Construction/Zoning Official calls the contact on the form to schedule. Call the Building Department to confirm permits are closed before the inspection.
resale_co.contact_title: Technical Assistant, Building Department (Construction Code Official: Mark Berninger, ext 213, mberninger@wclnj.com)

evidence.quote: No person shall occupy or use any portion of a residential building after such building or portion thereof has been vacated or sold, until the owner or landlord thereof shall have applied for and secured a resale certificate.
A resale certificate shall expire six months after the date of issuance.
The following fees shall be applicable for the inspection and issuance of a resale certificate including the smoke detector and carbon monoxide detector compliance.
Prior to the sale of any residential building or any portion thereof, the owner thereof shall apply to the Woodcliff Lake Building Department, on an appropriate form, for a Resale Certificate.
FORM MUST BE SUBMITTED NO LESS THAN 20 DAYS PRIOR TO CLOSING DATE
A Certificate of Occupancy shall expire ninety (90) days from issuance
Verify Sump Pumps are not piped into the sanitary sewer system and are discharged properly.
Public sidewalks & aprons will be required to be replaced if damaged or uneven (permit required).

resale_co.notes: Chapter 135 (Woodcliff Lake Resale Certificate Ordinance, Ord. No. 20-05 of 12-7-2020, amended 7-15-2024 by Ord. No. 24-14) was read through ecode360. Its fee section has no amounts in the online text, so the fees come from the Borough's current application form (PDF last modified February 2026), which has a poor text layer; some quotes (for example the two-family fee) were read from the page image and may not match an automated text check. The fee code (Chapter 163) still lists $100 for one-family homes, half the original fee or $50 for re-inspections, and an older $25 smoke detector compliance certificate fee. The form cites General Ordinance 131-5 and says the certificate expires in 90 days, while the code says six months. The CCO application PDF has a scrambled text layer, so the automatic quote check could not read it; the quotes were matched by eye to the PDF.

requirements: Smoke detectors UL approved, 10-year sealed battery, on each level including the basement, and within 10 feet of each sleeping area entrance or inside each sleeping area; hardwired alarms must be replaced with hardwired
Two-family homes also need alarms in common stairwells and hallways, outside each doorway, in the main living area, and at the front of the basement stairs
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of each sleeping area entrance or inside each sleeping area; the form says CO detectors older than 5 years must be replaced
All detectors must be less than 10 years old
Fire extinguisher 2A:10B:C, under 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen, with bracket, dated or tagged within 12 months (form still lists it)
Secondary power source label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the meter, if applicable
Central or low-voltage alarm systems need a passing alarm test and active monitoring

fire_cert.notes: Woodcliff Lake folds the smoke/CO certificate into the Resale Certificate (Section 135-7 says the fees cover the smoke and carbon monoxide detector compliance). The state directory spells the Fire Official's surname Maurrass and lists rmaurrasse@wclnj.com; the Borough page lists Raphael-Jose Maurrasse with fireprevention@wclnj.com. Other Fire Prevention contacts on the Borough page: Kyle Ladewig (x 225, kladewig@wclnj.com) and Diane O'Brien, Secretary (x 200, dobrien@wclnj.com). The form and Section 135-3 still require a portable fire extinguisher, which the state dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19). The form's 5-year CO detector replacement rule is stricter than the 10-year limit stated elsewhere in the same packet.
